items.s: Vijayanagara kingdom completely disappeared with this battle
items.x: After Talikota (1565) the Aravidus survived at Penugonda and Chandragiri; the civil-war Battle of Toppur (Topuru, 1616) broke up what was left, after which the empire disintegrated completely. Penugonda and Chandragiri were capitals, not the decisive battles.

items.s: In 1565 the Vijayanagar empire fell as a result of the war
items.x: The Vijayanagara empire's power was broken at the Battle of Tallikota (Rakshasi-Tangadi), 1565, by the Deccan Sultans; the capital then moved to Penugonda.

items.s: In the year 1565 the battle of Tallikota was fought between them?
o: The kings of Vijayanagara and the Sultanate of Golconda
Vijayanagar kings and Kondaveeti Reddy kings
Deccan Sultans and Kondaveeti Reddy Kings
items.x: Tallikota (1565) was fought between Vijayanagara under Rama Raya and the combined Deccan Sultans (Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar) – not Golconda alone and not the Kondaveedu Reddis, who had gone long before.

items.s: The Sufi saint of Naqshbandiya order, Ubaidullah Ahrar was followed by which among the following Mughal Emperor?
items.x: Babur was a follower of the Naqshbandi saint Khwaja Ubaidullah Ahrar; the order came to India with him.

items.s: Which Mughal Emperor wrote his own autobiography?
items.x: Babur wrote his autobiography, the Tuzuk-i-Baburi (Baburnama), in Turki; Akbar, Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb did not write autobiographies.

items.s: In which language was the Tuzuk-i-Baburi (Baburnama) written?
items.x: The Baburnama was written in Chaghatai Turkish; Persian was the Mughal court language.

items.s: Of which origin was the Rumi method of warfare used by Babur?
items.x: The Rumi method (carts linked as a barrier for matchlockmen and artillery) was Ottoman; Tulughma was Uzbek.

items.s: Where did Babur build the Kabuli Bagh Mosque to commemorate his 1526 victory?
items.x: The Kabuli Bagh Mosque is at Panipat and marks the 1526 victory; Ram Bagh was at Agra.

items.s: Which inviter of Babur was the Governor of Punjab?
items.x: Daulat Khan Lodi, Governor of Punjab, invited Babur along with Alam Khan and Rana Sanga.

items.s: What was Alam Khan, one of those who invited Babur, to Ibrahim Lodi?
items.x: Alam Khan was Ibrahim Lodi's uncle; Daulat Khan Lodi was the Governor of Punjab.

items.s: Of which origin was Babur's tulughma tactic, in which flanks wheel round to encircle the enemy?
items.x: Tulughma was Uzbek; the Rumi (araba) method was Ottoman.

items.s: Which cities did Babur occupy after the First Battle of Panipat?
items.x: After Panipat Babur occupied Delhi and Agra.

items.s: In which year did Babur take the title 'Padshah' at Kabul?
items.x: Babur became Padshah at Kabul in 1507 and took the title Ghazi after Khanwa in 1527.

items.s: After which battle did Babur take the title 'Ghazi'?
items.x: Babur took the title Ghazi after Khanwa (1527) and the title Padshah at Kabul in 1507.

items.s: During whose reign did the Mughal empire become a political fact and a factor in the life of India, influencing her ever since?
items.x: Under Akbar's long reign (1556-1605) the Mughal empire was consolidated by conquest, mansabdari and Rajput policy and became a lasting political fact in India.

items.s: During Akbar period, land revenue system “ Ain-i- Dahsala” was developed by :
items.x: Raja Todar Mal devised the Ain-i-Dahsala (1580), helped by Khwaja Shah Mansoor and Muzaffar Khan Turbati.

items.s: Who among the following was the connecting link between Sher Shah and Akbar in land revenue administrative measures ?
items.x: Raja Todar Mal served Sher Shah's revenue administration and then devised Akbar's zabt, so he was the link between the two.

items.s: With reference to Mughal period’s revenue collection system, ‘Zabti’ means
items.x:
Most keys: 1/3rd of total yield. Strictly zabt means the measurement-based cash assessment; one-third was the state's share under it.
Zabti assessed revenue on measured land at crop rates, with the state demand fixed at one-third of the average yield, hence the printed key. 'Estimate' describes kankut.

items.s: Which Mughal Emperor abolished the Persian Court Custom of ‘Sijda’ which was begun by Balban?
items.x: Shah Jahan abolished the court custom of sijda (prostration) begun by Balban, replacing it with the chahar taslim.

items.s: Which of the following Mughal Emperors wrote his autobiography in Persian ?
items.x: Jahangir wrote his autobiography, the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri, in Persian; Babur's Tuzuk-i-Baburi was in Turki.

items.s: The Mughal Emperor who prohibited the use of tobacco was
items.x: Jahangir banned tobacco smoking (1617), as he records in his memoirs; Akbar, Babur and Aurangzeb did not.

items.s: Which Mughal Emperor Started Hijri Samvat in India by replacing Illahi samvat?
items.x: Shah Jahan gave up Akbar's solar Ilahi era and restored the Hijri (lunar) reckoning for regnal years.

items.s: Which Mughal emperor abolished sijda (prostration before the emperor)?
items.x: Sijda, begun by Balban, was ended by Shah Jahan.

items.s: Which of the following statements about the Mughal emperors is correct?
o: Babur adopted the title Zinda Pir.
Shah Jahan received the title 'Shah Jahan' from Jahangir.
Aurangzeb was known as Nur-ud-din Muhammad Jahangir.

items.s: Which of the following describes Jahangir's religious policy?
o: A complete break from Akbar's tolerance
Broadly continuing Akbar's tolerance, though Guru Arjan Dev was executed for political reasons
items.x: Jahangir broadly continued Akbar's tolerance; Guru Arjan Dev was executed for political reasons linked to support for the rebel prince Khusrau.

items.s: Which Mughal emperor, slightly more orthodox than Akbar, destroyed some newly built temples yet kept many Hindu nobles?
items.x: Shah Jahan was slightly more orthodox and destroyed some newly built temples but continued to employ many Hindu nobles.

items.s: Which traditions does Dara Shikoh's Majma-ul-Bahrain bring together?
items.x: Majma-ul-Bahrain ('mingling of two oceans') compares Sufism and Vedanta.

items.s: Of which text is Dara Shikoh's Sirr-i-Akbar (1657) a Persian translation?
items.x: Sirr-i-Akbar is the Persian Upanishads (1657); the Mahabharata became the Razmnama under Akbar.

items.s: What is the meaning of the title ‘Shah Jahan’?
items.x: Shah Jahan means King of the World, a title Prince Khurram took on his accession. Alamgir means Conqueror of the World, Sakari Saka-conqueror and Devanampiya Beloved of the Gods.

items.s: Which one of the following emperors had the highest number of Hindu Generals in the Mughal army:
items.x: The Hindu share in the nobility was highest under Aurangzeb (about 31.6%, mostly Marathas from the Deccan wars), against about 22.5% under Akbar.

items.s: Which Mughal Emperor was known as "Zinda Peer" ?
items.x: Aurangzeb, simple and orthodox in his personal life, was called 'Zinda Pir' (living saint).

items.s: Who of the following Mughal Emperor was coronated twice?
items.x: Aurangzeb was crowned twice - at Delhi on 21 July 1658 and again on 5 June 1659 after Khajwa and Deorai.

items.s: The Mughal Emperor who appointed the maximum number of Hindu officials was –
items.x: Aurangzeb had the largest number of Hindu officials (about 31.6% of the nobility), mainly Marathas taken in during the Deccan wars.

items.s: Under Aurangzeb's jizya, children below what age were exempted?
items.x: Children below 14 were exempt, along with women, slaves, beggars and the unemployed.

items.s: Under which emperor did the Mughal Empire reach its maximum territorial extent?
items.x: Aurangzeb's Deccan conquests of Bijapur and Golconda gave the empire its greatest extent.

items.s: Under which Mughal emperor was the share of Hindu nobles in the nobility the highest?
items.x: Hindu nobles formed about 31.6% under Aurangzeb, against about 22.5% under Akbar.
